meaning: The smallest unit of text the model reads and writes. It can be one character, half a word or a punctuation mark, and the model only sees its ID number.
The program that cuts text into tokens and turns them into integer IDs. Every model ships with its own.
Picking one candidate token as the next output, using the probabilities the model gives.
Each step feeds everything generated so far back in to produce the next token, so an answer can only come out one token after another.
The "reading the prompt" stage: the model reads the whole question at once. The known tokens can be computed together, so it is fast.
The "writing the answer" stage: each new token depends on the one before, so tokens come out one at a time.
Storage stacked in layers, from fast and small to slow and large, with the most used data kept in the fastest layer.
How many bytes can move per second. Every output token reads a lot of parameters, so inference cares about it most.
The time you wait between sending a request and getting the result. You pay it even for a tiny amount of data.
A tokenization method: start from single bytes and repeatedly merge the pieces that often sit together into tokens.
The fixed format that adds role markers, a system prompt and so on to a conversation. The model reads the full text wrapped in the template.
The joint probability of a series of events equals the product of the conditional probabilities of each step. This is how the probability of a whole sentence is computed.
The probability that A happens, given that B happened, written P(A | B). The model outputs exactly this kind of probability at each step.
The raw scores the last layer gives each candidate token. They can be positive or negative, and become probabilities only after softmax.
Turns a list of scores into probabilities that are all positive and sum to 1. Subtracting the maximum first prevents overflow.
The number T that the scores are divided by before sampling. Below 1 makes answers more conservative; above 1 makes them more varied.
How a computer stores decimals: a sign, an exponent and a mantissa. The bit count is limited, so range and precision are limited.
A floating-point result exceeds the largest representable value and becomes infinity.
A special floating-point value meaning "not a number", such as ∞ ÷ ∞. Once it appears, it spoils every result that follows.
A way of writing an algorithm that is mathematically equivalent but does not overflow or badly distort results at finite precision.
Compute the cumulative probabilities, then find the first position that exceeds a random number u. This picks a token according to its probability.
No dice: each step picks the token with the highest probability, so the output is fully deterministic.
A sequence computed by a formula that looks patternless. Given the same seed, it can be reproduced exactly.
The starting point of the pseudorandom formula. The same seed gives the same sequence, so you can replay a run.
A list of numbers in a row. Between layers, every token in the model is represented as a vector.
A table of numbers with rows and columns. Most model weights are stored as matrices.
A block of numbers with coordinates. Vectors and matrices are tensors, and describing one needs both a shape and strides.
The length of each axis of a tensor. For example, a 2 × 3 matrix has 2 rows and 3 columns.
Multiply two equal-length lists of numbers element by element and add the results into one number. It is the basic step of matrix multiplication.
Every row of the matrix takes a dot product with the same vector. When you compute one token at a time, each weight is read once and used once.
Put several input vectors side by side and multiply them with the weights. Each weight is read once and shared by several tokens.
The number of each cell in memory. A program reads and writes data by address.
A layout that stores a table row after row in memory, so numbers in the same row have neighboring addresses.
A layout that stores a table column after column in memory, so numbers in the same column have neighboring addresses.
How many elements or bytes the address jumps when one coordinate grows by 1. With the shape, it decides where data sits in memory.
When a group of GPU threads reads neighboring addresses, the hardware merges the requests into a few large reads. This is much faster than scattered reads.
The bit in a floating-point number that says whether the number is positive or negative.
The bits in a floating-point number that record the power of 2. They set the range of values it can represent.
The bits in a floating-point number that record the significant digits. More bits mean higher precision.
The step size shared by a whole block of numbers in quantization. Multiply a code by it to recover an approximate value.
The integer stored for each number after quantization. It says the number is about this many times the scale.
The simplest quantization method: set the step from the largest absolute value in a block, then use equally spaced levels, symmetric around zero.
The gap between the value recovered after quantization and the original number. The coarser the step, the larger the error.
Square each error and take the average. It sums up the overall error of a block of numbers.
A single value far larger than the others in its group. It stretches the quantization step, so the other small numbers lose precision.
How many operations you do per byte moved. It decides whether a program is limited by bandwidth or by compute.
A chart that uses two "ceilings", bandwidth and compute, to show the fastest speed a computation can reach.
How many floating-point operations the hardware can do per second, measured in FLOPS.
The point on a roofline chart where the two ceilings meet. Below its arithmetic intensity, a program is bandwidth-bound; above it, compute-bound.
The longest chain from start to end in a dependency graph. Total time is at least that long, so only shortening it makes things faster.
The overall speedup is limited by the share that is not optimized. However fast one part gets, the total speedup has a ceiling.
The time from sending a request to seeing the first token. It includes queueing, reading the prompt and the first generation step.
The number of generated tokens divided by the time spent generating. It is not the final word count divided by the total time.
When many people use the system at once, the total number of tokens per second across all requests.
A model file format common in the llama.cpp ecosystem. It stores metadata and a tensor directory first, then the data.
Data about data, such as which architecture the model has and how many layers.
The directory in GGUF that lists each tensor's name, shape, data type and start position.
A named run of bytes on disk. The data must be loaded into memory before it can be computed on.
When memory or data is cut into equal blocks for management, each block is a page. Operating systems often use 4 KiB per page.
Attach a file to the program's address space. A page is read from disk only when it is used, so a successful mapping does not mean the data has been read.
The program touches a page that is not in memory yet. The operating system pauses the program, reads that page in, then lets it continue.
The operating system keeps file pages it has read in memory, so the next access does not read the disk again.
Tells the operating system not to move or swap out these memory pages, so the GPU can safely read them directly with DMA.
An integer type that holds only zero and positive numbers. It has a fixed number of bits and wraps around when it passes the limit.
An integer result exceeds the largest value its bits can hold and silently wraps to a small number, which can fool a bounds check.
A short number that summarizes a large block of data. Compare the two sides and you know whether the data changed.
A checksum algorithm that is sensitive to byte order. It is often used to find errors in transmission and storage.
A function such as SHA-256 that turns data into a fixed-length digest. It catches both accidental damage and deliberate tampering.
Change a single input bit and about half of the bits in the hash digest change.
A C++ idiom: an object frees its resources automatically when it is destroyed. It cannot control asynchronous work that is still using the resource in the background.
The list of numbers a token carries between layers. Each layer reads it in and writes out a list of the same length.
A nonlinear function applied to each number after a matrix multiplication. It lets a multi-layer network learn complex patterns.
The simplest activation function: negative numbers become 0, and positive numbers stay the same.
A function that squeezes any number into the range 0 to 1. It is often used as a "gate" that controls how far something opens.
The activation function z × sigmoid(z). It is like a smooth ReLU, with a slight dip in the negative region.
The attention layer in the Strata model. An indexer first picks the relevant earlier positions, and attention runs only on those.
How most layers of the Strata model look back. It compresses the earlier text into a fixed-size state, which is overwritten a little with each new token.
Divide a vector by its "size" so that the next layer receives numbers on a stable scale.
The square root of the sum of the squares of a vector's components. This is its geometric length.
The square root of the mean of the squares of the components. After RMS normalization, the average size of each component is 1.
Normalize by the root mean square, then multiply by a set of learned factors. The result differs from L2 normalization by a factor of √d.
Each layer computes only a correction and adds it back to the input: x′ = x + f(x). Information can pass through many layers almost unchanged.
The mechanism where the current token scores every earlier position, then mixes the earlier information by how relevant each position is.
The vector in attention that says "what I am looking for" at the current position. It is scored against every key.
The "label" vector of each earlier position in attention. It is compared with the query to decide how much that position is looked at.
The vector in attention that says "what content this earlier position can offer". The values are mixed by weight into the output.
Run many sets of queries, keys and values at once. Each "head" looks for its own kind of information, and the results are merged.
Rotate the query and key according to the token's position, so the model can tell order. The value is not rotated.
The attention rule that hides future positions. Each token can see only itself and the tokens before it, even while reading the prompt.
How the amount of work grows as the input grows. It is used to estimate how slow an algorithm is.
A notation that keeps only the "shape" of how work grows with input and ignores constants, such as O(n²).
Stores the keys and values computed at each earlier position in the attention layers, so they are not recomputed. The longer the conversation, the more space it takes.
Lets several query heads share one set of keys and values. This shrinks the KV cache.
A cheap scorer in QSA. It scores all earlier positions and picks a few for the real attention.
What a system remembers. At each step it is updated to a new state from "old state plus new input".
A model that is always in one of a limited number of states, and only specific events can switch it to another state.
A model that uses a trainable network to update a fixed-size state step by step from "old state plus new input".
Turns two vectors into a table whose entry in row i, column j is kᵢ × vⱼ.
The number of truly independent directions in a matrix. A table made by an outer product has rank 1.
Adding an outer product to a matrix. GDN uses it to write a key and value pair into the state.
Read the old value before writing, then write only the difference "target minus old value", so the new and old values do not pile up.
Each layer has many experts, and each token wakes only a few of them. The model has many parameters, but each step computes little.
In MoE, a group of parameters that performs one kind of transformation. What it is good at forms automatically during training.
The expert in each layer that every token uses. It is not chosen by the router.
The part of each MoE layer that scores all experts, picks the top few and decides their weights.
Pick the k highest scores from a list. When scores are very close, the result can change because of tiny errors.
The current input decides which parameters take part in the computation. Parts that are not chosen are not computed at all in this step.
A data structure whose top is always the smallest value. A min-heap that holds only k numbers finds the top k efficiently.
Uses the partition idea from quicksort to find the k-th largest number. On average it takes only linear time.
Approximate the original numbers with low-bit integers plus a shared scale. It saves space but adds error.
n tokens in a row. For example, the last 2 tokens form a bigram and the last 3 form a trigram.
A naive language model that guesses the n-th word by looking only at the previous n−1 words.
A rule that scrambles any input into a number that looks random but is the same every time. It is often used to decide where data goes.
In Strata's n-gram hash, the intermediate number made by multiplying each token ID by a constant and XOR-ing the results.
Two different keys hash to the same place. With fewer slots than keys, this must happen.
A structure that stores and reads data at the slot number computed by a hash function. Lookup is usually fast.
One slot in a hash table. Keys that hash to the same number all go into the same bucket.
Strata caches recently read n-gram table rows in memory, so it does not read the disk again and again.
The cache is split into many sets with 8 slots each. A piece of data can go only into one of the 8 slots of its own set.
Each set has a round-robin counter. On a miss, the slot it points to is replaced, and the pointer moves one slot on.
A cache where each piece of data can go into only one fixed slot. Lookup is fastest, but frequently used data easily pushes each other out.
A cache where data can go into any slot. It is the most flexible, but every lookup must compare against all slots.
A cache where data is first assigned to a set by a rule, then placed in any slot within the set. It is a compromise between direct-mapped and fully associative.
The share of lookups where the needed item is already in the cache. When you report it, say what the denominator is.
The set of data actually used in the recent period. The hit rate is high only if the cache can hold it.
The cache cannot hold the working set, so data is evicted just after it is loaded, and is moved back and forth again and again.
Strata first counts how often each expert is chosen and ranks them in a list. At the start, the popular experts from the list are placed in VRAM.
The rule that decides which old data to evict when the cache is full.
The theoretically best replacement policy: evict the item that will be used furthest in the future. It needs knowledge of the future, so it serves only as a reference.
First in, first out: the earliest arrival leaves first. It can be a cache replacement rule or a queueing order.
Least recently used: when the cache is full, evict the item that has gone unused the longest.
Least frequently used: evict the item with the fewest total uses. It cannot keep up when the hot items change.
A pointer sweeps around in a circle. Recently used items are spared once, and only unused ones are replaced. It approximates LRU at very low cost.
Make counts shrink in proportion over time, so old favorites fade slowly and new ones get a chance to rise.
The table in Strata's expert cache that records which VRAM slot each expert is in, or that it is not in VRAM. The GPU reads only by this table.
A function hands the work off and returns at once. The work runs in the background, so returning does not mean it is done.
The central processing unit. It has few cores, but each is smart and good at programs with complex control flow.
One instruction does the same operation on a whole row of numbers at once. The CPU uses it to compute several numbers at a time.
The graphics processing unit. It has many simple compute units and high-bandwidth VRAM, and is good at doing many copies of the same computation at once.
The GPU has a group of threads run the same instruction at the same time, each working on its own data.
A group of worker threads Strata starts on the CPU for experts that miss the cache. They are assigned by physical core and compute in parallel.
A later computation needs the result of an earlier one, so the two must run one after the other, not in parallel.
The address a program sees. The operating system and the CPU must translate it into a physical address before memory is really read.
The real location on the memory module. Devices that use DMA understand only this kind of address.
A slot in physical memory, cut to the page size, that holds one virtual page.
The table that records where each logical page actually sits in physical memory. Both the operating system and Strata's KV cache use one.
When memory is tight, the operating system writes rarely used pages to disk to free physical memory.
A small part inside the CPU that caches address translation results. When there are too many pages to fit, access slows down.
The part on a GPU that is dedicated to moving data. Copying can happen at the same time as computing.
The device reads and writes memory by itself, without going through the CPU. It understands only physical addresses.
The caller waits until the work is done before the function returns.
A clear notice that background work has really finished. The result of an asynchronous call can be used only after it arrives.
A work queue in CUDA. Work in one stream runs in the order submitted, and different streams need events to synchronize.
A signal that marks that something has happened. CUDA uses it to confirm that earlier work is done; in SSE it means a pushed message.
Prepare two buffers: while one is being computed on, the other loads the next piece, so the copying hides behind the computing.
A small program that does one core computation. The CPU launches it on the GPU, and many threads run it at the same time.
An independent line of execution in a program. Threads of one process share memory, and a GPU can run thousands at once.
A group of GPU threads that run on the same compute unit and can share a small piece of fast storage.
A group of 32 threads on an NVIDIA GPU. They run the same instruction at the same time.
The fixed cost for the CPU to prepare and submit a kernel. When the kernel is tiny, this becomes the main cost.
Merge several small operations into one kernel, which cuts the number of launches and the reads and writes of intermediate results.
Record a whole series of GPU operations first, then submit and replay the whole series at once. This saves the cost of launching them one by one.
Strata puts parameters that change every step, such as the position, into a small piece of VRAM, so a recorded graph reads the new values without being changed.
One piece of a long prompt. Each chunk goes through all layers before the next is read, and the chunk size affects speed and VRAM.
Split work into connected stages, so different parts handle different items at the same time. The total time is set by the slowest stage.
Cut logically continuous data into equal pages and use a page table to record where each page actually sits.
Cheaply guess a few tokens first, then have the large model check them in one batch. The correct guesses are accepted directly.
The candidate tokens that a cheap method guesses in speculative decoding. They count only after the target model checks them.
The large model that makes the final call in speculative decoding. The final output follows its judgment.
The part of a CPU that guesses which way a branch will go from history, so the pipeline need not stop and wait for the condition.
The CPU runs ahead in the guessed direction, but the results do not take effect yet. If the guess is right they are committed; if wrong, they are discarded.
Wrap several modification steps into one whole: either all take effect, or it is as if nothing happened.
Make temporary changes official and visible to the outside. Strata commits only the prefix that passed the comparison in the verification window.
Throw away the temporary changes and return to the state before the transaction began.
A multi-token prediction layer that comes with the model. In Strata it guesses the draft, and the large model still has to verify the draft.
A row made of the last confirmed token plus several draft tokens. The large model computes it in one pass and compares the tokens one by one.
The average result weighted by probability. Here it means the average number of tokens gained per round.
The probability that this position is accepted, given that all the earlier drafts were accepted.
A sum where each term is the previous one times the same number. This is why guessing more drafts gives less and less gain.
With each new data point, move the estimate a small step toward it. Older data gets less weight, and only one number needs to be stored.
In statistics, a case where the outcome was never observed. A draft that was never compared cannot be counted as a failure.
Find a passage in the context that repeats what is being written, and use the tokens that follow it as the draft.
The part at the start whose tokens are exactly the same as in the last request.
A prefix that was already read is not read again; the model continues from the break point. So a long conversation does not get slower and slower.
An optional Strata feature. When it is on, it changes the intermediate results of many layers in the model.
Save all the state at one moment so you can return to that moment later, like a game save.
The checkpoints in a Strata session are lined up by length, and each one is a prefix of the next.
Several parties first share one copy of the data, and a block is copied only when someone wants to change it.
Keeps track of how many users a piece of data has now. It can be freed only when the count drops to 0.
Cut the model's layers in order into several segments. Each GPU handles one continuous segment, and data is handed over only between segments.
In a layer split, the continuous segment of layers that one GPU handles.
Split the model by layers into segments on several GPUs. Data finishes one segment before it enters the next.
Split the big matrix of one layer across several GPUs and compute at the same time. Results are merged at every layer, so communication is frequent.
Each GPU holds a full copy of the model and handles different requests. It needs almost no communication between GPUs.
The time at the start and end of a pipeline when some stages have no work and can only wait.
The serial bus on the motherboard that connects the CPU, GPUs and other devices. Its bandwidth is far lower than VRAM.
One data line side by side in PCIe, like one lane of a road. ×16 means 16 lanes.
A dedicated high-speed link between NVIDIA GPUs. Its bandwidth is far higher than PCIe, and home dual-GPU setups usually do not have it.
The human-readable text of a program, written by programmers.
The binary instructions a chip really executes. Machine code for different chips is not interchangeable.
The rules for which instructions a chip can execute and how each is encoded, for example x86-64 and its AVX2 extension.
A program that translates source code into machine code for some instruction set. A different chip needs a new compile.
The step that edits the text before C/C++ is compiled: it pastes in header files, replaces macros and removes branches by condition.
A name defined with #define. During preprocessing it is replaced as is with the text it stands for.
Use #if to keep only one branch for the target. The compiler never sees the rest of the code.
An instruction that makes the CPU report which features it supports. The program uses it to pick a suitable kernel at run time.
NVIDIA's GPU programming platform. It includes C++ extensions, a runtime library and a compiler, and works only on NVIDIA GPUs.
AMD's GPU programming interface, modeled on CUDA. Most function names only swap cuda for hip.
A thin layer of code between two layers that smooths out their differences. Strata uses it to swap CUDA names for HIP names.
The connection stays open, and the server sends each piece as soon as it is written. Each piece ends with a blank line.
The translation layer between the engine and the application. It turns chat messages into tokens, and turns generated tokens back into text.
Split one answer into many small pieces and send each as soon as it is written, so the user sees the first word sooner.
The protocol browsers and servers use to talk: the client sends a request, and the server replies with a status code, headers and a body.
The number of each character in Unicode. For example, "é" is U+00E9.
A rule that writes a character's number as 1 to 4 bytes. A Chinese character takes 3 bytes and may be cut in half by the network.
In UTF-8, the bytes after the first byte of a character. They start with the binary bits 10.
A decoder that holds back an incomplete ending and waits for the next chunk to join it, which avoids garbled text.
A text format that uses curly and square brackets for structured data. The text must be complete before it can be parsed.
A running program with its own memory and resources. The operating system reclaims them when it ends.
A communication channel the operating system provides between processes: one end writes and the other end reads.
The outside only sets a cancel flag. The worker sees it at a checkpoint, cleans up after itself and then exits.
A shared mark that means "please stop". The worker checks it at agreed places.
The agreed place where the worker checks the cancel flag. At best, cancellation waits until the next checkpoint is reached.
Checks at intervals whether a part is still active. If it does not respond for too long, the part is judged to have failed.
Confirming "who you are", for example checking that the API key in a request is correct.
Confirming "what you may do". After authentication, it decides which operations are allowed.
A long random string that the server and client share in advance. A request must carry it to use the service, and it must be kept secret.
An attack that steals information from "by-products" such as timing or power use.
A side-channel attack that guesses a key bit by bit by measuring how long a comparison takes.
Compare the whole string and then return, no matter at which position the first difference is, so the time leaks nothing.
A malicious web page points its own domain name at 127.0.0.1 for a while, and uses that to reach services on your own machine.
The moment when an operation counts as taking effect instantly. A cancellation counts as effective only from this boundary on.
When several tasks compete for the same resource, deciding who is served first and for how long each time.
With first come, first served, one long task blocks all the short tasks behind it.
Shortest job first: always do the shortest task first. The average wait is shortest, but task lengths must be known in advance.
A task is overtaken by other tasks again and again and never gets served.
Each task takes a turn for one time slice. If it is not finished, it goes to the back of the queue.
The short stretch of time a task may run without a break in round-robin scheduling.
The mathematics of systems with "arrival, queueing and service". It is used to estimate waiting times and queue lengths.
The share of time the server is busy. The closer it gets to 100%, the faster the waiting time grows.
The average number of people in a system equals the arrival rate times the average time each person stays. It hardly depends on any assumption.
The simplest queueing model, with random arrivals, random service times and only one server.
Compute several sequences together, so each weight is read once and shared by several tokens.
Several sequences start together as one batch and end together. A short one that finishes writing still waits for the longest.
After every generation step, check whether any sequence has finished. As soon as a slot is free, a queued new sequence takes it.
Before accepting a sequence, reserve all the resources it needs at once. If they are not enough, it queues or is rejected.
The longer a request waits, the higher its priority. It is used to prevent starvation.
An independent source that can tell you what the correct result should be. Without one, a test can only check that the program did not crash.
A test of just one function or one class. It is small and fast, and when it fails it points to the problem exactly.
Connect several modules and check that both sides keep the interface contract between them.
A test that goes in through the user's entry point and checks the final result. Also called an end-to-end test.
Each time you fix a bug, keep a test that reproduces it, so it cannot come back later.
A fake object with controlled behavior that stands in for a real but expensive part, such as a fake engine when there is no GPU.
One unit at the last bit of a floating-point number. Changing the order of computation often shifts the result by one or two ULPs.
The error allowed when comparing two floating-point numbers. If they differ by little enough, they count as equal.
A tolerance scaled by the size of the number itself, for example allowing a difference of one in ten thousand.
A fixed error threshold, for example anything within 10⁻⁶ counts as equal. It also covers numbers close to 0.
Do not let the engine continue freely. Feed every side the same reference text and compare the predictions at each position.
A measure of how "surprised" the model is by a piece of real text. The lower it is, the more accurate the prediction.
Plant bugs in the code on purpose and see whether the tests catch them. It checks whether the tests themselves are reliable.
Feed the same inputs to the implementation under test and to an independent reference implementation, then compare the outputs of both.
When you do not know the correct answer, check whether a rule of the form "if the input changes this way, the output should change that way" holds.
How much work is done per unit of time. Here it means how many tokens are output per second; larger is better.
Add up all the numbers and divide by the count. A few extreme values easily pull it off.
The number in the middle after sorting. A few extreme values do not affect it.
The value that a given share of the data does not exceed. For example, p95 means 95% of requests are no slower than it.
A measure of how spread out the data is around the mean. Its square root is the standard deviation.
The square root of the variance. It has the same unit as the data, and a larger value means the data is more spread out.
Run the same task again and again under controlled conditions to measure performance. You need warm-up, repeats and a written record of the conditions.
The output speed one user sees for themselves. It is not the same as the total throughput of everyone together.
One feature running from entry to exit, where each layer does only the necessary bit but the whole path really runs.
Organizing parts into a whole that meets the needs under given constraints. It almost always means trading off several goals.
Paying one cost to get one benefit, for example trading VRAM for speed.
The engineering cost left behind for the sake of speed. It keeps piling up and must be paid back sooner or later.
